# Aegraph rules

<!-- GENERATED by rulegen (see tools/aegraph.bzl). Do not edit: `bazel test //pass/aegraph:aeg_rules_md_fresh` fails
     when this file is stale. Refresh it with `bazel run //pass/aegraph:aeg_rules_refresh`. -->

Every rule the engine can run, per group (a group is a `rules/<group>.rules` file; a hand-written rule joins the
group named by its file's `AEG_RULE_GROUP`). Inside a group the rules are listed in the order the engine tries them:
priority descending, then name. `simplify` replaces the class, `alt` unions an alternative that extraction may keep,
`choice` is an alt carrying a `?` assignment.

Proof tier: `bv-swept` = the rule's instances are LEC-checked by `aeg_prove_<group>_smoke` over widths
{1,2,3,8,16,65} (bounded evidence, not a proof for all widths); `native-unverified` = hand-written, covered by the
union-invariant fuzz and an equiv fixture only; `none` = the rule opted out.

A SUBTRACTED inner Sum flips the banks of what it brings in. An aegraph never frees an e-node, so flattening a k-long chain one link at a time would leave O(k^2) dead operands behind (a 900-wide Or cost 400k pool entries). Instead a link whose only reader is a cell of the same op (Ctx::chain_inner) leaves the work to that reader, and the top of the chain absorbs every single-use link below it in ONE firing: linear, and a wide chain ends as one banked cell, as in classic cprop. |

The bound is the range guard. An alt: `sim` prices the multiply by an immediate plus a shift below the divide, `synth` keeps the Div (the divider array specializes on a constant divisor and measured smaller than the multiplier of the magic constant: aeg_div_rem, area 4182 against 4637). Extraction on the example: synth keeps the left side; sim keeps the right side. |

An alt: both profiles keep the Div (a constant power-of-two divide is cheap in each: a shift in hardware, a shift pair in the simulator). Extraction on the example: synth keeps the left side; sim keeps the left side. |

The bound is required: the difference carries no width stamp of its own, so it is wrapped in a mask of clog2(c) bits (x % c < c), which gives bitwidth the bound the Rem had; and a dividend without a provable bound (bitfuzz clears the pins) is refused. An alt. Extraction on the example: synth keeps the left side; sim keeps the left side. |

| `getmask_lane` | simplify | 40 | Get_mask | native-unverified | mask.cpp:100 | Get_mask(x, lo, hi) where x's lane layout (a Concat, a Set_mask chain, a SHL, a packed Or/Sum of disjoint shifted fields) holds the whole window in one lane: read the lane's source instead, or zero for an empty lane. It is only rewritten when the lane layout of x holds that window in one lane of another class (or zero): the packed read an array element or a struct field makes (`m[3]` of a Set_mask / Concat word is a shift by the lane offset). A plain right shift of an unstructured value stays a shift, which costs one operation less than shift-and-mask. |
| `getmask_sum_chain` | simplify | 37 | Get_mask | native-unverified | mask.cpp:267 | A low window of a Sum reads its operands modulo 2^hi, so an operand that is itself a low window Get_mask(y, 0, k) of a Sum y (k >= hi) can be y: the sums merge into one wider Sum under the outer window, Get_mask(Sum(Get_mask(Sum(a, b), 0, 16), 1-), 0, 16) = Get_mask(Sum(a, b, 1-), 0, 16) (modular arithmetic: the truncation of the inner sum is undone by the outer one). Classic folds the same chain (`(base + size - 1)` of an address range). Only when every operand of y already fits `hi` bits, so the merged Sum is no wider than the outer window: a wide y would trade the inner mask for a wider adder. |
| `getmask_drop_terms` | simplify | 36 | Get_mask | native-unverified | mask.cpp:173 | A window of an Or / Xor / Sum / And does not read the terms that cannot reach it: * a term whose low `hi` bits are zero (a constant left shift by >= hi, a multiple of 2^hi) adds nothing to the bits below `hi` of an Or, Xor or Sum (a Sum carries only upwards), and zeroes the whole window of an And; * a non-negative term below 2^lo has no bits in [lo, hi): it adds nothing to an Or or Xor window and zeroes an And. The bit-gather ladder `((m[63] << 63) \| .. \| (m[1] << 1) \| m[0])[0]` reads one bit of 64 shifted rows, and classic's demanded-bits narrowing leaves only the row that owns the bit. Sole readers, or a window that keeps at most half of the terms, replace the read (simplify); otherwise the narrower Or is an alternative the extraction prices. |

The pieces are narrower than the lanes, so what feeds a lane is demanded at the window's width only. A Concat other readers keep alive is left alone: it exists either way and the re-pack would cost its lanes twice. |

| `or_shifted_windows` | alt | 21 | Or | native-unverified | mask.cpp:472 | Or of shifted windows of ONE word whose positions are contiguous in both the source and the destination: Or(x[a +: n] << s, x[a+n +: m] << (s+n), rest) = Or(x[a +: n+m] << s, rest) (a bare window is shifted by zero). Every shifted window is `x[lo, hi) << s`, so its bit lo+i sits at s+i; two windows with the same delta lo-s whose destination ranges touch tile one wider window exactly. This is the bit-gather ladder `(g[3]<<3) \| (g[2]<<2) \| (g[1]<<1) \| g[0]` that classic canonicalizes (pack canonicalization plus vectorize_bit_reductions) BEFORE a surrounding Or flattens it away; the engine's `flatten` merges nested Ors first, so without this rule a strided gather stays one shift and one Get_mask per bit. An alt: extraction keeps whichever form the profile prices lower. |
| `bit_run_reduction` | alt | 20 | And, Or | native-unverified | mask.cpp:402 | The per-lane form of classic vectorize_bit_reductions for its simplest family: an And (Or) with a run of at least four operands that are single bits of ONE word at adjacent positions, And(x[a], x[a+1], .., x[a+n-1], rest)  =  And(EQ(x[a +: n], 2^n - 1), rest) Or (x[a], x[a+1], .., x[a+n-1], rest)  =  Or (Ror(x[a +: n]), rest) (each operand is a 0/1 value, so the AND is "every bit of the window set" and the OR is "any bit set"). An alt: the extraction keeps whichever is cheaper, and the classic region pass still vectorizes the shapes that need a whole expression over the bits (Or(EQ(request[j], 0), priority[i][j])). |
| `getmask_shl_straddle` | alt | 20 | Get_mask | bv-swept | mask.rules:33 | A window that straddles the shift: the zero bits below, x's low hi - s bits above (the bitwidth_rewrite Get_mask(SHL) rule). An alt: both spellings are two nodes, so extraction keeps the original until a cost profile prefers the narrower Get_mask. |
| `setmask_to_concat` | simplify | 20 | Set_mask | native-unverified | mask.cpp:688 | Set_mask(base, lo, hi, v) over a pack (zero, a Concat, a value that fits below the window) whose lanes the window covers whole, or extends, is the pack with that lane replaced: a chain of constant, disjoint lane writes (a packed array or struct built field by field) becomes one Concat, as classic's pack canonicalization makes it. A write that cuts a lane in two, or a base that is anything else, keeps the Set_mask. |
| `or_pack_to_concat` | alt | 19 | Or | native-unverified | mask.cpp:564 | Or of fields at DISJOINT constant windows, each a value of known width optionally shifted left by a constant: Or(a << 8, b << 4, c)  =  Concat(a, w_a, b, 4, c, 4)       (w_a, 4 and 4 the widths; gaps are zero lanes) Classic's canonicalize_or_pack (the bit-gather ladder `(m[63] << 63) \| .. \| m[0]` of a packed row). An alt: the profile prices a constant shift and a Concat as wiring (synth) or as one instruction per lane (sim), and an Or of n shifted fields as n - 1 gates, so the original stays when a field is shared and the Concat would not be cheaper. Every field needs a proven width (unsigned_bits) and the windows must not overlap, or the rule declines. |

| `mux_setmask_pair` | alt | 35 | Mux | native-unverified | mux.cpp:109 | Both arms rewrite the same lane of the same word: select only the lane value, Mux(s, Set_mask(b, w, v0), Set_mask(b, w, v1)) = Set_mask(b, w, Mux(s, v0, v1)) (classic scalar_mux factor_set_mask_pair). It removes the word-wide Mux of a nested `if (reset) bit = R; else if (enable) bit = D;` update. An alt since milestone I: the lane Mux is narrower (hardware pays per bit, so `synth` takes it whenever the window is narrower than the word) but a simulator word is a word, and the factored form adds a Get_mask, so `sim` keeps the word Mux of a register of at most 64 bits. |

| `mux_const_arm_logic` | simplify | 30 | Mux | native-unverified | mux.cpp:41 | One constant 0/1 arm over a 0/1 value is plain logic: s ? 1 : f = s \| f      s ? 0 : f = !s & f      s ? t : 0 = s & t      s ? t : 1 = !s \| t Only over a computed (e-node) value: a latch Q is a leaf here, and `s \| q` on a latch's hold arm would be a Q -> D path through logic. |
| `mux_sel_arm` | simplify | 30 | Mux | bv-swept | mux.rules:4 | Mux(s, 0, s) = s: s ? s : 0. |

| `mux_guard_accumulation` | simplify | 25 | Mux | native-unverified | mux.cpp:178 | Guarded accumulation (classic scalar_mux guard_accumulation), a ROLLED-LOOP rule: `if s { acc OP= x }` is Mux(s, a, a OP x) = a OP Mux(s, id, x)      (id = 0 for Or/Xor, -1 for And; and the swapped arms) bit for bit the same logic, but the Mux no longer sits on the accumulator, so an unrolled run of guarded updates becomes one chain of ONE associative operator that flattens into a single n-ary cell instead of a serial mux chain. It runs only in a lifted loop body (Ctx::guard_scope), where bitwidth follows and sizes the new Mux; the update cell must be private to this Mux and plain (no color, no policy); a held STATE output stays a Mux (the latch contract exempts Q only as a direct Mux arm, and enableopt turns a Q hold into an enable). A Sum is not guarded: a + Mux(s, 0, x) puts the select ahead of the carry chain. |
| `mux_lane_vector` | alt | 20 | Mux | bv-swept | mux.rules:19 | One lane of a bit-sliced mux. Mux(s, x[a], y[b]) is bit (a mod 64) of the 64-bit-aligned word mux Mux(s, x[a0 +: 64], y[b0 +: 64]), with the same alignment offset on both arms. Every lane of a run that shares s, x, y and the offset b - a builds the SAME word mux, so hash-consing shares it among the lanes (classic vectorize_bit_muxes does this on the extracted graph; this is the alternative the extraction can pick once a cost profile prices the sharing). An alt: a lane alone is cheaper as the scalar mux. Extraction on the example: synth keeps the left side; sim keeps the left side. |
| `mux_oob_sel` | alt | 20 | Mux | native-unverified | mux.cpp:152 | Q1: an out-of-range or disconnected selection of an n-ary Mux is a '?' owned by that Mux, so any value is a legal resolution of it: a constant selector that names no connected arm may be read as 0 (classic folds exactly this to 0). Written as an alt, not a simplify: the engine never picks a refinement on its own, the extraction does, and a '?' that is one value to the Mux class stays one value at every reader (the literal is the Mux's own). |
